reviews.author: Yebin Kim
reviews.text:
I tried both the grilled mackerel rice bowl and the salmon sauce rice bowl and it was a satisfying meal!

In the grilled mackerel rice bowl, the mackerel was really plump, crispy on the outside, and moist on the inside, so it was savory with almost no fishy taste. The rice is topped with green kimchi and crunchy toppings, so when you mix it together, you get a variety of textures and never get tired of it. The seasoning was just right and not too strong.

The salmon paste rice bowl was thick and fresh, so it wasn't fishy and soft. The salty soy sauce goes well with rice, making it a great drink! The soba and side dishes that came with it were also neat, so it felt like a well-balanced meal overall.

The store was clean and the menu items were plentiful, so it was nice to have a filling meal. I recommend it if you like fish rice bowl :)

reviews.text:
It is a Pitzeria that started under the name of Del Horno in front of Hanyang University and has been operating for 5 years in the Wangsimni commercial district. Gornizone presents a canotto-style Neapolitan pizza with a puffy crust.

I have been interested in it for a long time, as it stands shoulder to shoulder with the leading pizzerias in downtown Seoul. However, I personally do not prefer the thick type of wood-fired pizza, so I postponed my visit.

In addition to pizza, it also serves various dishes such as pasta and has the status of a fancy Italian restaurant. They seem to be focusing all in on pizza and paying attention to the completeness of the entire menu, not just the assortment.

The wine list is also quite diverse and includes expensive wines. Even though it is a university town, demand for wine seems to be naturally forming as professors rather than students visit the place more often.

Since it was our first visit and there were only two people, we gave up on pasta and ordered two pizzas to share. There was a detailed explanation on the monitor, and the pizza price range was quite high, averaging around 20,000 won.

The pizza was also served with beer, Kölsch-style beer from Wangsimni Meznine Brewing Company. Even though it was an ale, unlike the Kölsch I had encountered so far, it was less clean like a lager and closer to a pale ale.

The first pizza that came out was a spicy Margherita topped with diavola, pepperoncino, and spicy salami. Since this is a pizza with a large portion of dough, I ordered it because I thought it would be nice to have more spiciness.

When I ate it while it was warm, the moistness of the olive oil, pepperoncino oil, and tomato sauce blended perfectly with the dough. The salami was grilled until it was crispy, adding a texture that contrasted with the dough, and the quality was excellent.

The dough had a rich flavor from the oven fire and firewood, and the gorniczone was thick but high and crispy. Thanks to this, I dipped it in the olive oil and peperoncino oil that was left on the bottom and it was really attractive.

The next pizza is Punggi, aka mushroom pizza. An earthy and creamy sauce made from ground button mushrooms was spread instead of tomato paste, and topped with oyster mushrooms, mozzarella, and provolone.

Overall, it had a much lighter and more greasy taste than Daabola, and since Provolone is a hard and sweet cheese, it gave off a heavy flavor. Maybe that's why the dough felt a little more filling.

There was fried wood ear mushroom in the center of the pizza, and at first I thought it was an artichoke. It was small and didn't seem to have much presence, but it had a nice crunchy texture and smoky flavor, so it went well with the dough in one bite.

Pizzeria Dalforno: The moment you feel Italy with just one pizza

This house… I really mean it.

I don't know where to start, but let's start with pizza.
This pizza looked like a margherita. The moment you take a bite, you will be surprised.
“Oh, Basil is alive?”
Cheese, tomato sauce, and basil harmonize like the holy trinity, and the crispy outside and chewy inside dough completes everything.
Really, I am thrilled to be able to taste the wood-fired pizza freshly baked in Naples in Korea.

The pasta was a work of art (especially that carbonara and ragu tagliatelle)

✔ Carbonara:
It is an authentic Roman style with a real ‘egg base’, not cream.
The savory flavor of grilled pancetta bacon on top of the chewy, non-greasy noodles was crazy.
Don’t use too much pepper, just give it a “pleasant stimulus” and you’re done.
Perfect balance even when consumed without alcohol.

✔ Ragù tagliatelle:
This… The taste of real beef made by boiling it for a long time.
Finely shredded meat and tomato-based sauce wrap around the wide tagliatelle noodles.
After taking one or two bites... I see myself scraping my plate.

Cream pappardelle cannot be left out.

The wide side catches the soft cream sauce, and the flavor of the shiitake mushrooms and button mushrooms is really deep.
It is not a thick cream, but a subtle and clean cream, so you can eat it until the end without getting tired of it.
A menu that will probably impress mushroom lovers.

⸻

🪑 Perfect atmosphere & service
• The store was quiet and calm, but the atmosphere was not too stiff so you could talk comfortably.
• The staff were very friendly, and the tempo at which the food came out was just right.
• You can feel the care put into the water cups, tableware, and even plating.
• They put neat paper mats on each table. It's a small thing, but it makes me feel good.

⸻

📌Overview

🔥 Pizza: 10 out of 10 (true Neapolitan feel)
🍝 Pasta: 9.8 out of 10 (Carbonara, Ragu, and Pappardelle all have different appeal)
🪑 Atmosphere: Dates, family gatherings, friends are all OK
💰 Cost-effectiveness: This price for this quality? Honestly it feels cheap
📷 Insta-worthy: Visuals that become works of art just by looking at the camera.

reviews.text:
After eating a pastrami sandwich at Medieval and heading home, I remembered that I had forgotten to stop by After Drink Burger, a new Smashed Burger restaurant nearby, after eating tsukemen at Mentendo near Wangsimni Station, so I decided to stop by as the route was right.

I saw it on Instagram and it was fortunate that it was open today, the last day of the Lunar New Year holiday. I stood in front of the store on the main street and saw a sign saying it was break time, so I was shocked, but just in case, the store door was opened and there were two people there. I asked if I could just eat one burger and they told me to come by, so I breathed a sigh of relief.

The menu only had four types of burgers and one type of chicken tender on the wall, but I remember reading in one review that the owner chef said that he was still refining the A.D.B. Burger, which felt like a signature menu item. I also liked the basic menu, so I asked for the classic burger as a separate item.

I thought the two of them went to the kitchen to cook, and after waiting for a while, they brought me a classic burger on a plate with a logo on it.

Visually, I didn't see anything special, but when I lifted the top bun, I saw chopped onions, cheese, pickles, and mayonnaise. I held it well and took a bite. The bun was not dry at all, but was soft and moist. Unless it's a sloppy restaurant, all patties are at a certain level. I don't think it's any more special than a Korean beef patty, but it's seasoned reasonably well and, like at the old supermarket white burger stand, it goes straight to the plate when you bite into it. It's moist enough even though it's not dripping with juice.

However, the pickles I was concerned about were sweet pickles rather than the dill pickles found in McDonald's Big Macs, so I was disappointed as I don't like sweet pickles in hamburgers, but since sweet pickles are so standard in Korea, they are not common outside of more American-style stores like One Star Old Fashioned Hamburger or Fat Boys, so I wasn't disappointed.

After eating deliciously and saying hello, I left Gagel.

Overall, I stopped by because it was a newly opened Smashed Burger store near Wangsimni Station, but it wasn't something I wanted to revisit on purpose. It was a store similar to the ones I visited recently, Bubbuk near Sungkyunkwan University or Smash Cheeseburger near Yeoksam Station. It was a restaurant full of passion worth stopping by if you wanted to try a burger when you were nearby, so I said it was delicious with my heart of support.
